title: Print Header Footer Navbar Spacing Parity
description: In the Zwischenbericht mit Bestand print report, the header (navbar) and footer chrome spacing no longer matches the on-screen app UI's navbar/footer spacing. The header currently has too little vertical spacing (too cramped) and the footer has way too much spacing (too much gap). Need to bring both back into parity with the app UI's navbar/footer padding, likely by adjusting headsep/footskip and/or internal chrome bar padding in print/tex/semio-window.sty (see SemioChromeNavbarHead, SemioChromeFooterHead, headsep=\semio@spacing@double, semio@chrome@footer@reserve computation around line 2621-2634).
summary:
Third follow-up: after the row@height fix, the header still looked squeezed with the rule sitting inside/against the chips instead of below them with a clean spacing-unit gap.

Root cause: in the very first fix of this ticket I had replaced the original hardcoded `\setlength{\headheight}{38.14006pt}` (print/tex/semio-window.sty) with a formula-derived `\semio@chrome@navbar@height + hairline` (≈20.46pt), reasoning it was a stale magic number. That reasoning was wrong: fancyhdr's own runtime page-assembly check (`Package fancyhdr Warning: \headheight is too small (20.46002pt): Make it at least 38.14006pt`) showed the *original* 38.14006pt was the empirically-correct value the previous author had already tuned to fancyhdr's real requirement — my "fix" was a regression that undersized the reserved header zone, causing my later `\vskip\semio@spacing@single` chip-to-rule gap (from the previous two rounds of this ticket) to be swallowed/invisible because there wasn't enough headheight for it to render into without the rule visually crowding the chip. Restored `\headheight` to the original `38.14006pt` and kept everything else (the row@height formula fix and the `\vfil` + `\vskip\semio@spacing@single` chip-anchoring in both `\semio@chrome@navbar@bar` and `\semio@chrome@footer@bar`, both from the two prior close-and-reopens of this ticket).

Also spent significant time chasing red herrings before finding this: (1) confirmed via a `--skip-nx-cache` "vskip 1cm" stress test that the vskip/vfil box mechanics genuinely work (produced an exactly-matching "Overfull \vbox (21.82263pt too high)" warning), ruling out a box-construction bug; (2) hit an unrelated, transient build failure from a concurrent session's in-progress edits to print/tex/semio-core.sty and print/tex/semio-window.sty (window-break-suffix / termlist-labels work, confirmed via `git diff` — untouched by me, and had already stabilized/auto-committed by the time of the final verification build).

Verified via `--skip-nx-cache` rebuilds of the real mit-bestand zwischenbericht document and all print/dist templates (report, paper, flyer, forschungsbericht, zwischenbericht, kompaktbericht): the `Package fancyhdr Warning: \headheight is too small` warning is gone, and rasterized header/footer crops show a clean, visible, matching gap between the chips and their rule in both bars, on both scrreprt and scrartcl templates.
